accepted.question_text: For a k-orbit abstract polytope—meaning an abstract polytope whose automorphism group has k orbits on flags—suppose one is given a distinguished generating set for its automorphism group analogous to the standard generators used for regular polytopes. What condition on those generators should replace the string C-group intersection condition so that the generator data still captures the polytope structure?

evidence.quote: Problem 1. Given a distinguished generating set for the automorphism group of a k-orbit polytope, what analogue of the intersection condition holds?

accepted.question_text: Given a general k-orbit polytope together with a distinguished generating set for its automorphism group, describe a construction that rebuilds the polytope as a coset geometry of that group, in the same spirit that regular and chiral polytopes can be reconstructed from suitable generator data.

evidence.quote: Problem 2. Describe a way to build a general polytope as a coset geometry of its automorphism group, given a distinguished set of generators.

accepted.question_text: The quotient criterion says, in regular and chiral settings, that under suitable facet hypotheses a regular cover is again polytopal. Find a combinatorial criterion, usable for arbitrary polytopes or maniplexes rather than only regular or chiral ones, that plays the role of this quotient criterion.

evidence.quote: Problem 3. Find a combinatorial analogue of the quotient criterion.

accepted.question_text: Characterize exactly which abstract polytopes P have monodromy group Mon(P) that is a string C-group, so that the minimal regular cover obtained from Mon(P) is itself polytopal.

evidence.quote: Problem 4. Give a characterization of the polytopes P such that Mon(P) is a string C-group.

accepted.question_text: Either find an abstract polytope P whose monodromy group Mon(P) is not a string C-group but which nevertheless has a unique minimal regular polytopal cover, or prove that no such polytope exists.

evidence.quote: Problem 5. Find a polytope P such that Mon(P) is not a string C-group, but P does have a unique minimal regular polytopal cover; or show the non-existence of such a polytope.

accepted.question_text: Given a string group generated by involutions, determine the minimal string C-groups that cover it.

evidence.quote: Problem 6. Given a string group generated by involutions, determine the minimal string C-groups that cover it.

accepted.question_text: For k-orbit polytopes with k ≥ 3, define the right analogue of the chirality group: a group-theoretic invariant that measures how far the polytope is from being regular and behaves well despite the fact that different flag stabilizers may have different normalizers.

evidence.quote: Problem 7. Determine the “correct” way to generalize the chirality group to k-orbit polytopes.

accepted.question_text: Given an abstract polytope P, determine the size of its monodromy group |Mon(P)|.

evidence.quote: Problem 8. Given a polytope P, determine | Mon(P)|.

accepted.question_text: Characterize exactly which pairs of rooted polytopes have a mix that is itself polytopal rather than merely a rooted maniplex.

evidence.quote: Problem 9. Give a characterization of pairs of rooted polytopes whose mix is itself a polytope.

accepted.question_text: For every pair of integers k ≥ 1 and n ≥ 3, does there exist a k-orbit n-polytope such that no rank-2 section is a digon?

evidence.quote: Problem 10. Are there k-orbit n-polytopes for every k ≥ 1 and every n ≥ 3 such that no section of rank 2 is a digon?

accepted.question_text: Given a group Γ, determine all pairs (k, n) with k ≥ 1 and n ≥ 3 for which Γ occurs as the automorphism group of a k-orbit polytope or of a k-orbit maniplex of rank n.

evidence.quote: Problem 11. Given a group Γ, what are the numbers k ≥ 1 and n ≥ 3 such that Γ is the automorphism group of a k-orbit polytope or maniplex of rank n?

accepted.question_text: Call a properly edge-colored n-regular graph allowable when it is connected and, for every colors i and j with |i-j| > 1, every walk with color pattern i, j, i, j returns to its starting vertex. Is every allowable graph the symmetry type graph of some maniplex?

evidence.quote: Problem 12. Is every allowable graph the symmetry type graph of some maniplex?

evidence.quote: Problem 13. Are there constructions of (n + 1)-polytopes P from n-polytopes where the symmetry type graph of P is different from those in Theorem 4.2 and from their duals?

evidence.quote: Problem 14. Which (combinatorial) symmetry type graphs occur among convex polytopes? Which geometric symmetry type graphs occur?

accepted.question_text: Do there exist abstract polytopes P and Q such that there is at least one amalgamation R with all facets isomorphic to P and all vertex-figures isomorphic to Q, while the polytope P itself has at least two non-isomorphic vertex-figures?

evidence.quote: Problem 17. Classify all pairs of polytopes P and Q such that hP, Qi is non-empty and the number of flag orbits of polytopes in hP, Qi is bounded.
